``` r
library(gtropic)
```

G-TROPIC is a global collection of tropical cyclone exposure data, published
on Harvard Dataverse and updated weekly. For every storm since 1980 in the
International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship (IBTrACS), it records
which second-level administrative units (ADM2) the storm came near, and the
wind, precipitation and flooding each unit experienced. It combines IBTrACS
tracks with ERA5-Land precipitation, Groundsource flood polygons, GHSL
population and geoBoundaries ADM2 units. `gtropic` retrieves, filters and maps
these data. It returns the published values as they are and recomputes nothing.

This vignette runs a first query and explains what comes back. The
[data sources](https://sparklabnyc.github.io/gtropic/articles/data-sources.html)
article on the package website describes the sources, their update schedules
and the helpers that list the available years, places and storms.

## A first query

`gtropic_data()` is the main function. This call retrieves every table for the
storms that formed in 2025 and came near the United States:


``` r
usa_25 <- gtropic_data(WHO_ENTITY = "United States", date_range = 2025)
#> Retrieving 0 files (0.0 B); 10 already cached.
#> Warning in fetch_hazards(args, ctx, scope, date_spec): No non-missing precipitation values were returned for 7 selected ADM2 units.
#> ! "52423323B10065184809144", "52423323B18524543454126",
#>   "52423323B37020317002794", "52423323B47905601981877",
#>   "52423323B81395860012193", "52423323B84565222808084", and
#>   "52423323B95364314409049"
#> ℹ A known current source-data limitation can affect small or coastal ADM2 units
#>   when no ERA5-Land grid cell is assigned.
#> ℹ A future G-TROPIC dataset release is planned to fill these gaps using
#>   finer-resolution ERA5 precipitation data.
#> ℹ See `?gtropic_known_limitations`; complete identifiers are available from
#>   `gtropic_diagnostics()`.
#> Warning in fetch_hazards(args, ctx, scope, date_spec): The raw flood data from Groundsource consists of polygons of places named in
#> news reports about flooding, rather than detailed flood maps.
#> ! As noted by Groundsource, flood data is both spatially and temporally biased,
#>   such that flood events in regions and time periods with more accurate
#>   reporting are over-represented while those lacking in news coverage are
#>   under-represented.
#> ℹ As such, care should be taken when interpreting and utilizing G-TROPIC flood
#>   exposure metrics. See `?gtropic_known_limitations`.
#> This warning is displayed once per session.

usa_25
#>
#> ── G-TROPIC data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Historical dataset: doi:10.7910/DVN/EAVWC3 (version 1.0)
#> • Genesis dates: "2025-01-01" to "2025-12-31"

#> • wind: 1068 rows x 12 columns
#> • precip: 4272 rows x 3 columns
#> • flood: 661 rows x 7 columns

#> • pop: 803 rows x 6 columns
#> • storm_metadata: 10 rows x 4 columns

```

The printout gives the dataset version, the genesis dates covered, how many
storms and units were selected, and the size of each table. `summary()` adds
the resolved filters and any diagnostics:


``` r
summary(usa_25)
#>
#> ── G-TROPIC data summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>
#> ── Sources ──
#>
#> • Server: "dataverse.harvard.edu"
#> • Historical dataset: doi:10.7910/DVN/EAVWC3 v1.0
#> • Files retrieved: 10 (189.1 MB)
#> • Retrieved at: 2026-11-26 17:16:27 UTC
#>
#> ── Tables ──
#>
#> • wind: 1068 rows x 12 columns
#> • precip: 4272 rows x 3 columns
#> • flood: 661 rows x 7 columns
#> • zero_pairs: 314381 rows x 5 columns
#> • tracks: 682 rows x 10 columns
#> • pop: 803 rows x 6 columns
#> • storm_metadata: 10 rows x 4 columns
#> • adm2: 803 rows x 5 columns
#> • geometry: 803 rows x 2 columns
#> • codebook: 7 entries (list)
#> • links: 1068 rows x 12 columns
#>
#> ── Resolved filters ──
#>
#> • ADM2 units: 803
#> • Storms: 10
#> • Genesis window: 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31
#> • Wind radius: 500 km
#> • Precipitation window: -2/ +1 days within 500 km
#> • Flood window: -2/+1 days within 500 km (match: "start")
#>
#> ── Warnings ──
#>
#> • precip_all_missing_adm2_ids: 52423323B10065184809144,
#> 52423323B18524543454126, 52423323B37020317002794, 52423323B47905601981877,
#> 52423323B81395860012193, and ... and 2 more
#> • flood_reports: The raw flood data from Groundsource consists of polygons of
#> places named in news reports about flooding, rather than detailed flood maps.
#> As noted by Groundsource, flood data is both spatially and temporally biased,
#> such that flood events in regions and time periods with more accurate reporting
#> are over-represented while those lacking in news coverage are
#> under-represented. As such, care should be taken when interpreting and
#> utilizing G-TROPIC flood exposure metrics. See ?gtropic_known_limitations.
```

Three defaults shape the result:

- `wind_radius_km = 500` keeps wind records for unit-storm pairs whose storm
  track passed within 500 km of the unit's population-weighted centroid.
- `precip_radius_km` and `flood_radius_km`, also 500 km, do the same for
  precipitation and floods.
- `precip_days_before = 2` and `precip_days_after = 1`, and their flood
  equivalents, keep rainfall and floods from two days before to one day after
  the storm's closest approach to each unit.

These values do not define "exposure"; choose them for your study. `Inf` or
`NULL` removes a radius. `vignette("filtering")` and `vignette("linkage")`
cover them in detail.

## The returned object

A `gtropic_data` object is a named list of tibbles:


``` r
names(usa_25)
#>  [1] "wind"           "precip"         "flood"          "zero_pairs"
#>  [5] "tracks"         "pop"            "storm_metadata" "adm2"
#>  [9] "geometry"       "codebook"       "links"
```


``` r
usa_25$wind
#> # A tibble: 1,068 × 12
#>    ADM2_ID  STORM_ID LOCAL_DATETIME_STORM…¹ LOCAL_DATETIME_MAX_W…² STORM_DIST_KM
#>    <chr>    <chr>    <chr>                  <chr>                          <dbl>
#>  1 5242332… 2025185… 2025-07-06T14:00:00-0… 2025-07-06T05:00:00-0…         152.
#>  2 5242332… 2025223… 2025-08-16T22:00:00-0… 2025-08-16T22:15:00-0…         196.
#>  3 5242332… 2025280… 2025-10-10T07:15:00-0… 2025-10-10T09:45:00-0…         277.
#>  4 5242332… 2025185… 2025-07-07T09:45:00-0… 2025-07-07T13:45:00-0…          11.4
#>  5 5242332… 2025215… 2025-08-02T14:00:00-0… 2025-08-02T15:00:00-0…         471.
#>  6 5242332… 2025243… 2025-09-09T19:30:00-1… 2025-09-09T20:45:00-1…         311.
#>  7 5242332… 2025185… 2025-07-07T14:00:00-0… 2025-07-07T12:45:00-0…          75.1
#>  8 5242332… 2025185… 2025-07-07T14:00:00-0… 2025-07-07T12:30:00-0…         108.
#>  9 5242332… 2025185… 2025-07-04T08:15:00-0… 2025-07-06T04:00:00-0…         358.
#> 10 5242332… 2025185… 2025-07-07T00:15:00-0… 2025-07-07T03:00:00-0…          77.9
#> # ℹ 1,058 more rows
#> # ℹ abbreviated names: ¹​LOCAL_DATETIME_STORM_CLOSEST, ²​LOCAL_DATETIME_MAX_WIND
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: VMAX_SUST_MS <dbl>, SUST_DUR_MINUTES <dbl>,
#> #   VMAX_GUST_MS <dbl>, GUST_DUR_MINUTES <dbl>, WIND_RADII_VMAX_SUST_MS <dbl>,
#> #   WIND_RADII_SUST_DUR_MINUTES <dbl>, LOCAL_DATE_STORM_CLOSEST <date>
```

| Table | One row per |
| --- | --- |
| `wind` | unit and storm with nonzero wind, within `wind_radius_km` |
| `precip` | unit and local date inside a storm's precipitation window |
| `flood` | unit and place named in a flood news report, matched to a storm's flood window |
| `zero_pairs` | unit and storm with no measurable wind |
| `pop` | unit and year: population and population-weighted centroid |
| `tracks` | storm-track observation |
| `storm_metadata` | storm: identifiers, name and genesis date |
| `adm2` | unit: names and country and WHO classifications |
| `geometry` | unit boundary, as an `sf` object (needs the `sf` package) |
| `codebook` | the dataset's own documentation, as a nested list |
| `links` | unit and storm; see below |

The codebook describes every column, its units and its provenance. Pass a
shorter `tables` vector to download and hold less.

> **Current precipitation limitation:** Some small or coastal ADM2 units may
> have no non-missing precipitation values because no ERA5-Land grid cell was
> assigned. Retrievals and automatic map captions identify affected units; see
> `?gtropic_known_limitations` for details and the planned dataset correction.

> **Flood data limitation:** The raw flood data from Groundsource consists of
> polygons of places named in news reports about flooding, rather than
> detailed flood maps, and is both spatially and temporally biased by news
> coverage. `PROP_AREA_IN_FLOOD_REPORT` and `PROP_POP_IN_FLOOD_REPORT`
> (published as `PROP_FLOODED_AREA` and `PROP_FLOODED_POP`) are the share of a
> unit inside one reported place, not its flooded area or population.
> `gtropic_data()` warns about this once per session; see
> `?gtropic_known_limitations`.

## The links table

`links` has one row per unit-storm pair inside the largest requested radius:


``` r
usa_25$links
#> # A tibble: 1,068 × 12
#>    STORM_ID      ADM2_ID      LOCAL_DATE_STORM_CLO…¹ STORM_DIST_KM WIND_EXPOSURE
#>    <chr>         <chr>        <date>                         <dbl> <lgl>
#>  1 2025185N30280 52423323B10… 2025-07-06                     152.  TRUE
#>  2 2025223N17337 52423323B10… 2025-08-16                     196.  TRUE
#>  3 2025280N11319 52423323B10… 2025-10-10                     277.  TRUE
#>  4 2025185N30280 52423323B10… 2025-07-07                      11.4 TRUE
#>  5 2025215N33284 52423323B10… 2025-08-02                     471.  TRUE
#>  6 2025243N14239 52423323B10… 2025-09-09                     311.  TRUE
#>  7 2025185N30280 52423323B10… 2025-07-07                      75.1 TRUE
#>  8 2025185N30280 52423323B10… 2025-07-07                     108.  TRUE
#>  9 2025185N30280 52423323B10… 2025-07-04                     358.  TRUE
#> 10 2025185N30280 52423323B10… 2025-07-07                      77.9 TRUE
#> # ℹ 1,058 more rows
#> # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​LOCAL_DATE_STORM_CLOSEST
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: WIND_IN_FIELD <lgl>, PRECIP_IN_FIELD <lgl>,
#> #   PRECIP_WINDOW_START <date>, PRECIP_WINDOW_END <date>, FLOOD_IN_FIELD <lgl>,
#> #   FLOOD_WINDOW_START <date>, FLOOD_WINDOW_END <date>
```

It gives the local date of closest approach (`LOCAL_DATE_STORM_CLOSEST`), the
distance (`STORM_DIST_KM`), whether the pair lies inside each hazard's radius
(`WIND_IN_FIELD`, `PRECIP_IN_FIELD`, `FLOOD_IN_FIELD`), and each precipitation
and flood window. Precipitation and flood records are returned once each, even
when a day or an event falls inside two storms' windows, so assign them to
storms by joining through `links`: `vignette("linkage")` shows how to do that
without double counting.

## Query metadata


``` r
# The published files used, at which dataset versions
gtropic_manifest(usa_25)
#>
#> ── gtropic version manifest ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Server: "dataverse.harvard.edu"
#> • Historical dataset: doi:10.7910/DVN/EAVWC3 (version 1.0)
#> • Files recorded: 10
#> • Total size: 189.1 MB
#> • Retrieved: 2026-11-26 17:16:27 UTC
#> • Package version: "0.0.0.9002"
#>
#> ℹ Pass this object as `manifest` to `gtropic_data()` to
#> reproduce the same retrieval.
```


``` r
# The filters as the package resolved them
gtropic_filters(usa_25)
```

``` r
# What the query warned about
gtropic_diagnostics(usa_25)
#> $precip_all_missing_adm2_ids
#> [1] "52423323B10065184809144" "52423323B18524543454126"
#> [3] "52423323B37020317002794" "52423323B47905601981877"
#> [5] "52423323B81395860012193" "52423323B84565222808084"
#> [7] "52423323B95364314409049"
#>
#> $flood_reports
#> [1] "The raw flood data from Groundsource consists of polygons of places named in news reports about flooding, rather than detailed flood maps. As noted by Groundsource, flood data is both spatially and temporally biased, such that flood events in regions and time periods with more accurate reporting are over-represented while those lacking in news coverage are under-represented. As such, care should be taken when interpreting and utilizing G-TROPIC flood exposure metrics. See ?gtropic_known_limitations."
```

The manifest replays the same retrieval later, even after the dataset has been
revised (`vignette("versions-and-caching")`). `gtropic_availability()` records
the sources' update schedules and known coverage. These drive the warnings a
query may give, for example about provisional IBTrACS data for recent storms,
the few days' lag of ERA5-Land precipitation, or the end of the flood record on
2026-01-22.

## Larger queries

Downloads are kept in a cache between sessions, and a query estimated to need
more than 1 GB of new downloads asks before it starts; in a script it stops
instead, unless you pass `confirm = FALSE`. `vignette("versions-and-caching")`
covers both.
